title: Anthropic Reports $16.8B Q3 Revenue as Growth Slows From 145% to 45% Ahead of IPO
summary:
Anthropic told prospective investors at a San Francisco presentation on Wednesday that third quarter revenue rose about 45% from the prior quarter to $16.8 billion, slowing from a roughly 145% jump in the second quarter, when sales climbed to $11.6 billion from $4.7 billion in the first quarter. The Claude developer reported positive free cash flow, an 85% adjusted gross margin, and an adjusted operating margin above 11%, marking its second straight quarter of adjusted profitability as it prepares for an initial public offering as soon as November.

The company told attendees it generates $1.70 in revenue for every $1 spent on compute and outlined more than $500 billion in computing and infrastructure spending over the next decade. Rival AI labs distilling Claude outputs accounted for 5% to 7% of revenue, or more than $840 million in the third quarter, before Anthropic moved to curb the practice. Some prospective IPO investors now favor a valuation below $1.5 trillion rather than the $2 trillion floated by bankers, while Anthropic's pre-IPO perpetual contract on Liquid fell more than 10% over the past month to below $2 trillion.

The deceleration in quarterly growth weighed on AI hardware shares, extending a selloff in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index to a seventh straight session—its longest losing streak since May 2025—and erasing more than $2 trillion in market value over that span. The index fell 3.6% on Thursday to its lowest level in nearly a month, with Intel down 5.9%, Marvell off 5.5%, AMD falling 5% and Nvidia down 3%.

selectedTweets.bestBit: A good chunk of the market seems to want to read Anthropic's lower than expected ARR as a sign that demand slowed because Anthropic's models are falling behind.
selectedTweets.text:
A good chunk of the market seems to want to read Anthropic's lower than expected ARR as a sign that demand slowed because Anthropic's models are falling behind.

So where did that demand go? Open source? No. It went to OpenAI. Didn't everyone already watch people cancel Claude en masse and move to Codex when Astra came out?

Expectations were just too high. Total demand didn't change. You have to look at the combined ARR of OAI and Ant, not at either company on its own.

Wasn't this trade never really about how much money OpenAI or Ant makes? Wasn't it about how much these two companies spend, and sizing who benefits from that spending?
